I also agree entirely with you, but let's not kid ourselves: Blizzard is setting the bar here, and they have a fully automated system that bans people based on an algorithm, with no human oversight, and (very publicly) no appeals system. Unless they are just incredibly inept, false positives will be a small percentage of the banned userbase, so it's easy to ignore and/or outright slander them to silence opposition, which is exactly what they've been doing. It saves time and resources, both of which translate directly into dollars. Other companies will be scrambling to implement a similar system.

It is true that human oversight is slim to none in this current iteration of the system, but while the likelihood of being wrongfully banned is very low, if it does happen to enough people and there is no manner in which it can be reviewed or overturned they are going to end up with a group of very angry consumers.
